notes.1: The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C. From the Data Booklet the element is gallium. When three electrons have been removed, the electronic configuration of the Ga3+ ion is 1s22s22p63s23p63d10. The third shell is full at this point. Therefore, the removal of the fourth electron, giving Ga4+, is from a filled shell.
notes.21: The most commonly chosen incorrect answers were B and C. This suggests that many candidates did not appreciate the significance of the phrase ‘has a branched carbon skeleton’, and they included one or both of pentan-2-ol and pentan-3-ol. However, the only compound with molecular formula C H O, a branched carbon skeleton and a secondary alcohol group, is 3-methylbutan-2-ol.
notes.30: The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was D. From the infra-red spectrum, K clearly has a C=O group but no COOH group; it is therefore an aldehyde or a ketone. This rules out D. The conditions stated in the question would oxidise an aldehyde to a carboxylic acid. Therefore, K is a ketone and J must be a secondary alcohol. The answer cannot be B as this structure does not have a branched chain. Therefore, the answer is C.
notes.34: The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was B. Choice B would mean statements 1 and 2 are correct. However, statement 1 cannot be correct as there is no gas produced in this reaction. Statement 2 refers to the ‘disappearing cross’ experiment, so this statement is true. Statement 3 is also true as the reaction causes a decrease in the concentration of ions present. The answer is therefore C.
notes.39: The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C. This was a challenging question involving careful • If compound 1 undergoes an addition reaction with steam, butane-1,3-diol is produced. If this is oxidised, 3-oxobutanoic acid is produced. Statement 1 is therefore true. • If compound 2 undergoes a substitution reaction with OH–, 3-hydroxybutanoic acid is produced. If this is oxidised, 3-oxobutanoic acid is produced. Statement 2 is therefore true. • If compound 3 undergoes a substitution reaction with OH–, 3-hydroxybutanal is produced. If this is oxidised, it gives 3-oxobutanoic acid. Statement 3 is therefore true. All three statements are true, so therefore the answer is A.
notes.key_messages: • Candidates should avoid the early rounding of intermediate answers during calculations. • Candidates are reminded that observations for a chemical reaction should focus on the physical changes that take place. • The use of the Data Booklet should be encouraged for questions involving infra-red spectra. • When a question asks for a name of a reagent(s) then the formula of reagent(s) is not acceptable.
